children: National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) shares rose as much as 5.21 per cent on their trading debut on Thursday, extending gains after listing at a premium to the issue price.
NSE shares started trading at Rs 1,800 per share on the BSE, up 0.84 per cent from the issue price of Rs 1,785. The stock later climbed to Rs 1,878, up 5.21 per cent from the issue price.
The gains placed NSE among the world's 10 largest listed exchanges and India's 10 biggest companies by market value.
Analysts expect further upside in the stock, with brokerages setting price targets of up to Rs 1,965 per share.
PL Capital initiated coverage on NSE with an 'Accumulate' rating and a price target of Rs 1,950 per share, implying an upside of about 9.2 per cent over the issue price.

"Market dominance in cash and futures to continue; share erosion in index options to be a drag. Expect ~11 per cent revenue and PAT CAGR over FY26-29E; EBITDA margin to normalize to 76 per cent as one-offs get adjusted," PL Capital said in its report.
The brokerage said NSE dominates the exchange landscape with more than 93 per cent share in the cash market and nearly 100 per cent in stock and index futures.
It said NSE's market share in index options has declined to around 65 per cent due to regulatory hurdles, while the introduction of CAS and proprietary trading rules has further impacted volumes.
While revenue grew at a 25 per cent CAGR during FY21-26, PL Capital expects growth to moderate to an 11 per cent CAGR over FY26-29E due to the shrinking share in index options.

The brokerage expects NSE's EBITDA margin to recover to 76 per cent by FY29, from 71 per cent in FY26, as the impact of one-off costs fades. It expects PAT to grow at an 11 per cent CAGR during the period.
PL Capital said NSE's IPO values the company at Rs 4.4 lakh crore, with a price-to-earnings multiple of 32 times based on FY29E earnings. It said the valuation largely captures the premium.

The report highlighted NSE's position as a market leader in the Indian exchange landscape, its diversified growth engine and the expected recovery in EBITDA margin as the impact of one-time costs fades.
Macquarie also initiated coverage on NSE with an 'Outperform' rating and a target price of Rs 1,965 per share.
The target price implies an upside of about 10 per cent over the IPO issue price of Rs 1,785.
Macquarie described NSE as "The Dominator", citing its leading market share, comprehensive suite of services, technology infrastructure and deep liquidity.

The brokerage said these attributes make NSE a key part of India's ongoing financialisation. "Entrenched network effects, industry-leading profitability and cash" underpin its positive outlook on the exchange, Macquarie said.
